MTA-A1.title: Euclid's algorithm and its number of steps
MTA-A1.description: Find the GCD with Euclid's algorithm and count how many "division with remainder" steps the algorithm made. This lets you observe the algorithm's effectiveness and finiteness properties.
MTA-A1.instructions: Input: a b. Output: the GCD and the number of steps on one line (every pass with b ≠ 0 is one step).

MTA-A2.title: Fibonacci numbers: recursion with memory
MTA-A2.description: Plain recursion F(n) = F(n−1) + F(n−2) takes exponential time because the same values are computed again and again. Store the computed values (memoization) to bring the complexity down to O(n).
MTA-A2.instructions: Input: n. Output: F(n), where F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1.
MTA-A2.constraintsText: 0 ≤ n ≤ 90 (the result fits in a long).

MTA-A3.title: How many times a value occurs in a sorted array
MTA-A3.description: In a sorted array find the first and last positions of x with binary search (the lower and upper bounds). Their difference is the number of occurrences of x. Every query is O(log n).
MTA-A3.instructions: Input: n; n numbers (in non-decreasing order); q; q queries. Output: for every query, on its own line, the number of occurrences.

MTA-A4.title: Heap sort (heapsort)
MTA-A4.description: Turn the array into a heap (a max-heap), then move the largest element to the end and restore the heap. The complexity is O(n log n), extra memory O(1). Write it without a ready sort function.
MTA-A4.instructions: Input: n; n integers. Output: the numbers sorted in ascending order.

MTA-A5.title: The number of swaps in bubble sort
MTA-A5.description: Bubble sort swaps neighbouring elements that are in the wrong order. The number of swaps equals the number of inversions in the array (pairs i < j with aᵢ > aⱼ). Compute it.
MTA-A5.instructions: Input: n; n numbers. Output: the number of swaps.

MTA-A6.title: Balanced brackets (a stack)
MTA-A6.description: A line consists only of the brackets ( ) [ ] { }. Check with a stack that the brackets open and close correctly: an opening bracket is pushed onto the stack, and a closing bracket must match the one on top of the stack.
MTA-A6.instructions: Input: one line. Output: Muvozanatli (balanced) or Muvozanatsiz (not balanced) — the answers are in Uzbek, that is how the tests check them.
MTA-A6.constraintsText: The line is 1 to 10^5 characters long.

MTA-A7.title: Dijkstra's algorithm: shortest distances
MTA-A7.description: In an undirected graph with non-negative weights find the shortest distance from vertex s to all vertices with Dijkstra's algorithm. With a priority queue (a heap) the complexity is O((n + m) log n).
MTA-A7.instructions: Input: n m; m lines u v w (an edge and its weight); s. Output: on one line the distances to vertices 1..n; -1 if unreachable.

MTA-A8.title: The Fenwick tree: sum queries
MTA-A8.description: Do two kinds of operations on an array quickly: adding a value to an element and finding the sum of the range [l, r]. A Fenwick (binary indexed) tree does both in O(log n); a plain loop takes O(n) per query.
MTA-A8.instructions: Input: n; n numbers; q; q lines add i x or sum l r (indices from 1). Output: the result of every sum query on its own line.
